note: Adversarial redundancy test: how much of the predicate layer could the existing consensus layer have produced? Consensus is given every advantage (best of four metrics, ties resolved in its favour, predictors fitted on the same films they are scored on). Read-only; nothing merged.

pairOverlapEqualBudget.verdict: Consensus's best metric (idfOverlap) recovers 1580 of 7299 predicate pairs (21.6%) at equal budget, against 1254 expected at chance — lift 1.26x.

wellKnownOnly.note: Restricted to the films consensus says it knows WELL and for which it declared attributes, so a missing overlap is a judgement rather than a silence. This is the version most favourable to consensus.

strongestPredicateEdgesOnly.note: The predicate edges strong enough to have any chance of a visible slot, against an equal-size consensus draw.

rankRecovery.question: If you rank a film's 291 co-cohort films by consensus similarity, where do its predicate partners land?

vocabularyDuplication.method: For every predicate on >=6 cohort films, the best consensus predictor is searched over all 59 attributes, all 1,711 two-attribute ANDs and all 1,711 two-attribute ORs, fitted and scored on the same films. This overfits in consensus's favour deliberately: the F1 is an upper bound on what a consensus rule could have achieved.

selectivity.question: A predicate is a selector. How selective is a consensus attribute by comparison?

predicatePrevalenceOverCohort.measuredOn: 300 films of the 300-film stratified Pass A cohort — all above the 1,500-char evidence floor by construction. The corpus is 2,204 films of which 657 (29.8%) are below that floor and can never be tagged, so this is a prevalence over the READABLE corpus estimated from a stratified sample, not a corpus prevalence.

predicatePrevalenceOverCohort.note: Recorded, NOT cut. The band cut belongs after full-corpus tagging (frozen file, afterPassC).

inBandAttributeCoOccurrenceRule.rule: both films hold, at weight >= 0.5, at least one consensus attribute whose corpus prevalence is inside the predicate band 0.4-8% — i.e. consensus used exactly the way a predicate is used

edgesWithZeroConsensusAttributeOverlap.note: The honest figure is the second: the rest involve one of the 15 films consensus declined to describe, which is a coverage gap, not a disagreement.
